content.text: I have enough to conclude. No take-or-pay, minimum purchase, shortfall, or volume-cap provisions exist; payments are upfront/milestone/royalty (success-based), and AbbVie manufactures its own supply at its own election.

input.quote: 3.6 Expenses and Invoicing. Except as expressly set forth in this Agreement, each Party shall bear all costs and expenses associated with the Development activities for which such Party is responsible under this Agreement and the Initial Development Plan
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty, or volume cap on AbbVie (our party), so it sits at the preferred position. Searches for "minimum", "shortfall", "commit to purchase", "purchase" and "supply" return no commitment language: the only "minimum" references are insurance limits (Sections 11.6.1(b)-(c)), and there is no obligation for AbbVie to buy any quantity of Licensed Compound or Product from Harpoon. To the contrary, Section 4.5.1 gives AbbVie "the sole right, at its expense, to Manufacture (or have Manufactured) and supply the Licensed Compound and Licensed Products for commercial sale," with a manufacturing technology transfer available on AbbVie's request (Section 4.5.2), so supply volumes are entirely at our election. AbbVie's payment obligations are the Section 6.1 upfront fee and success-based development/regulatory milestones and royalties on Net Sales (Sections 6.2-6.3), which are event- and usage-linked rather than guaranteed minimum spend, and Section 3.6 allocates development costs to the responsible Party rather than committing AbbVie to a floor. Section 4.2 is a Commercially Reasonable Efforts diligence covenant, not a volume commitment, and remedies are limited to a good-faith discussion process. Nothing to redline for this rule; commitments running from Harpoon to us are outside the rule's scope.
